findings.reason: without a bound on repeat aborts or an exclusion for a deliberate quote, the guard can livelock a turn that must mention the markup (the nodes writing §3's own tests and fixtures do).
findings.text: the guard ends the stream on a structural opening in any tool input, so a turn whose input legitimately quotes the markup is aborted; §3's own justification for the structural matcher is that "this plan's own census and fixtures quote the bare token", but the cited fixtures carry structural openings (`<｜DSML｜ calls>`, `<｜DSML｜ invoke name="Bash">` in `fixtures/leak-*.json` and `clean-*.json`), and §1 excludes this plan's own runs from the census precisely because their tool inputs carry the markup on purpose — so legitimate structural quotes are known to occur, and a retried turn that re-writes the same quoted text is aborted again, which no bound or exclusion in §3 prevents.

findings.reason: §5's closing measure rests on a receipt distinction that s3's change removed, so the node that lands §5 would have to invent the count or report it unproducible.
findings.text: §3 records a firing as `STATUS_ABORTED`, "as a cut does, so no receipt reader counts a new status", while §5 (depends-on s3) measures "the receipts' guard status" and "the number of guard firings the receipts record" over the window after the restart; because the receipt now carries no marker separating a guard firing from an operator pause, §5's promised count cannot be produced from the receipts, and the per-firing log line §3 adds — the only attributable source — is not named by §5.
